cells.tense: What you have been tending is bearing fruit now, and you are here to see it.
cells.ask: Write down what you tended that got here, one line, and set aside one new thing to start.
cells.core:
You know how to keep something alive until it gives back more than you put in. That shows up as showing up — at the right intervals, in the right amount, while nothing is visibly happening yet. The result in front of you reads as if it were inevitable. It wasn't. You kept it going.

What's here now is abundance, and it is a kind of pressure too. Weeds are work, harvest is work, and it is very easy to move straight from the last task to the next tender thing without once standing still in front of what grew. The ground here holds everything that hasn't happened yet. Don't crowd it. Finish what's ripening, then leave some of that space empty on purpose.
cells.sheetLine: What grew is in front of you. Stand in it a while.
cells.verb: tending what grows until it can be gathered
cells.place: the ground before anything has been planted or named

cells.tense: You are already at the harvest that hasn't happened yet, reaching past what is actually ripe.
cells.ask: Pick one patch and tend only that one this week, leaving the other starts untouched.
cells.core:
You can grow things. That part works, and it has worked often enough that you now treat ahead-of-schedule as normal. Somewhere ahead is the full garden, the clear result, the thing that finally accounts for all of it — and you are already living there, static and rich, before any of it is ready. Stretching toward that picture is the only tending you have left.

What that costs is this: young things get pulled up to check their roots. The harvest you have gets picked hard and often before it's ready. You can hold back the extra reach for one week and still be the one who grows it. Whatever you're imagining ahead, the patch in front of you is the one you can touch tonight.

cells.tense: You are standing where nothing has been planted yet, and you are not planting anything.
cells.ask: Put one small thing in soil today, something that needs no special tools or skills, and let it be enough.
cells.core:
The ground is there. What isn't happening is anything going into it. When a possibility shows up, even a good one, you hold it at a distance — you look at it, you weigh it, you think about what it would take, and you don't begin. Ideas aren't scarce, and once something is underway you can carry it. The starting is what's absent, the putting of something into the ground where it could actually grow.

You don't need to relight the whole thing at once, and nobody is asking you to trust any of it yet. One seed is enough to test the ground. Small, cheap, and finished in a day.
cells.sheetLine: The ground is still there. You just stopped planting.

cells.tense: You are already growing something without admitting that you chose to start it.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one thing you keep showing up for is yours, and name what you're testing about it.
cells.core:
You're cultivating something. It's regular, it's on time, it happens whether you feel like it or not — and the way you talk about it, it sounds like circumstance rather than a decision you made. The growing is real and it's working. Only the fact that you chose it is unfiled.

That gap isn't harmless. When what grows gets credited to luck or timing, you don't get to rest in it, because on some level you don't believe you made it. So you keep going back to check on it, and each visit costs a little energy that was already earned. Naming it takes no effort and returns the energy you're still spending on not knowing. One sentence, spoken, closes the gap.
cells.sheetLine: You're already growing it. You just haven't claimed it.
